posts.title: Load Management and Electrical Supply Planning for Workplace Car Parks
posts.excerpt: Understanding how physical site assessments and dynamic load management prevent costly supply upgrades in commercial car parks.
posts.content:
When businesses evaluate electric vehicle charging for staff or commercial fleet vehicles, the most common engineering question concerns electrical capacity. Facilities managers frequently assume that introducing multiple charging points requires expensive, disruptive utility supply upgrades. Since founding Kodou Charging in Northfield in 2017, our engineering team has assessed hundreds of commercial car parks. In the vast majority of workplaces, existing distribution infrastructure can support a robust charging installation when planned through methodical site surveys and intelligent load balancing.

Every successful workplace project begins with a physical 90-minute site assessment visit. During this survey, site assessor Tomas Reyes inspects the facility distribution board, measures incoming supply headroom, and maps physical cable containment routes across the building structure. Rather than relying on theoretical estimations, this survey verifies the exact electrical load profiles of heating, cooling, machinery, and lighting circuits. Within 5 working days of the visit, we deliver a comprehensive technical report and fixed quotation valid for 60 days. The initial assessment fee of €290 covers up to 12 parking bays, with each additional 12 bays assessed at €120, and the entire €290 fee is credited against the installation invoice when work proceeds.

The cornerstone of efficient workplace charging is managing power when building demand peaks. Our €640 load-management module continuously monitors the main electrical intake of the property. When high-power equipment or central plant systems draw peak current, the module dynamically trims power to connected vehicles. As building consumption subsides during late afternoon or evening hours, charging points automatically return to full capacity. This dynamic throttling ensures that 7.4 kW wall units and twin-socket posts operate safely without ever exceeding the main fuse thresholds of the property.

Hardware selection must reflect how vehicles use the car park throughout the working day. For staff car parks where employees remain on site for full work shifts, 7.4 kW wall units mounted to perimeter walls or structural concrete pillars deliver steady, dependable charging. In depot yards and logistics facilities, ground-mounted twin posts placed along kerb islands allow two commercial vans to charge simultaneously from a single cable route. This practical configuration was recently demonstrated at the Harlow Lane print depot, where 4 twin posts serving 14 van bays were installed across 3 days on site, keeping commercial delivery vehicles charged overnight without disrupting daily printing production.

A similar balance was achieved at Brightwell Offices, where 8 wall units across 36 staff bays were installed in 2 days on site, and at Northfield Health Centre, where 3 twin posts serving 6 visitor bays were commissioned in a single day. Installation lead Amara Okafor and fitter Owen Castell coordinate all cabling and mounting to ensure parking bays remain accessible during physical work, which typically lasts between 1 and 3 days. Following installation, Sofia Lund coordinates our annual service programme, priced at €180 per site plus €25 per unit, which preserves ongoing electrical safety and operational compliance.

Workplace electrification does not require complex disruption or unbudgeted infrastructure overhauls. By combining an accurate 90-minute technical assessment, calibrated load-management modules, and tailored commercial hardware, businesses can install reliable vehicle charging that fits neatly within existing electrical capacities. Facilities managers wishing to review their car park infrastructure can reach our client desk at Unit 4, 18 Lantern Street, Northfield, to arrange an on-site survey.
